questions.question: Define fascism and list six features of a fascist state, giving an example of each from Nazi Germany.
questions.expected_answer: Fascism is an extreme authoritarian nationalism first established by Mussolini in Italy in 1922. Features: extreme nationalism (Germany above all; racial superiority); a single leader (the Führer principle); one-party state (all other parties banned in July 1933); suppression of opposition (Gestapo, SS, concentration camps); propaganda and censorship (Goebbels's ministry, book burning, People's Receiver radios); militarism and expansion (rearmament, conscription in 1935, lebensraum); control of the economy (Four-Year Plan, German Labour Front); control of youth (Hitler Youth compulsory in 1939).

questions.question: Describe how the Nazi state controlled young people and women, and how some people resisted.
questions.expected_answer: Schools taught Nazi history and racial biology with Nazi teachers; boys joined the Hitler Youth and girls the League of German Girls, effectively compulsory from 1936 and legally from 1939. Women were told their role was children, kitchen and church, were pushed out of professions and rewarded for large families with loans and the Mother's Cross. Resistance came from groups such as the Edelweiss Pirates, the White Rose student leaflets and Confessing Church pastors such as Niemöller and Bonhoeffer.

questions.question: Compare a fascist state with a democracy under four headings, using South Africa's Constitution as the example of democracy.
questions.expected_answer: Power: fascism concentrates it in one leader; democracy separates it between legislature, executive and independent judiciary. Parties and elections: fascism allows one party; democracy has free and fair elections with many parties every five years. Rights: fascism removes them and imprisons opponents without trial; South Africa's Bill of Rights protects equality, dignity, expression and fair trial, enforced by the Constitutional Court. Media: fascism controls and censors it; democracy guarantees a free press. Citizenship: Nazi Germany based it on race; South Africa guarantees equality for all.
